text:
Emil Heineman's season in one play: a turnover in the corner, an open net, and a shorthanded goal that put the Islanders ahead in Winnipeg this week. He's a north-south winger who goes to the net and finishes what lands there.

His line reads modestly, 3 goals and 9 points in 21 games at about 15 minutes a night. Underneath, the Islanders break even with him on the ice at five on five (49.6% of expected goals, our measure of chance quality), and results with him out there have run 10.2 goals better than the chances. That gap is the biggest luck sign on his card, and it tends to close.

His own role is clear. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 86th percentile among forwards for chances from the home-plate area last season, and a 90.8 mph top shot gives those looks teeth. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level in 2025-26 because his team created little offense with him on the ice. Watch whether the hits (52 already) keep coming with chances attached.
